decision.outer_island_first: Rejected as centerline. Tarawa strengthens caution, but attacking Taroa/Wotje/Mili one by one would expose the fleet longer to the same Japanese air/submarine/carrier network.

US_fast_carrier_centerline.composition_note: 5 CV + 6 CVL Branch TF58; Lexington CV-16 and Independence remain unavailable, while Wasp CV-7 survives in this branch.
US_fast_carrier_centerline.principle: Tarawa learning increases suppression/recon/direct-fire allocations but does not remove anti-carrier CAP/search, ASW, oiler protection or deck-cycle constraints.

Tarawa_learning_applied: more photo/submarine/reef reconnaissance and repeated battle-damage assessment
larger bombardment ammunition reserve and permission to re-engage supposedly neutralized positions
stronger beach traffic control and wreck-removal planning
more close-support destroyer availability, with explicit loss of those hulls from outer SG/ASW screen when committed inward
finite_capacity_guards: More shells do not multiply destruction linearly; target identification, smoke/dust, fire sectors and landing safety cap useful rate.
More LVT/LST create reserve depth faster than usable beach frontage; lanes, exits, refueling and disabled-vehicle clearance can congest.
Four operational Japanese first-line carriers force a real fleet-defense/search reserve.
The assault date is not delayed to await Lexington because further delay increases Japanese construction, submarine and carrier preparation.
